headline: Elected Nicole LaBrecque chair and Chris Carrigan vice chair; tabled the clerk position until September.
summary: Members discussed the Green Community Festival on September 19, 2026, and will invite green companies to take part. Members and staff also gave updates on projects, including the pedestrian bridge and the San Remo area plan. Officers were elected, and the clerk position was tabled.
decisions: Elected Nicole LaBrecque as Chair and Chris Carrigan as Vice Chair, unanimously.
Tabled the Clerk position until the September meeting.
Directed members to reach out to green companies to invite them to the Green Community Festival.

plain_text:
Page 1 
Economic Development Committee 
August 11, 2026  
The South Burlington Economic Development Committee held a regular meeting at 5:30 PM 
in Room 301 of the South Burlington City Hall, 180 Market Street, South Burlington and by 
remote participation.  
Members present:  Nicole LaBrecque (Chair), Chris Carrigan (Vice Chair), Harold 
Hershberg, Paige Brochu, John Burton and Brad Krompf.  
Members absent:  Emma Shouldice-Boardman, Rebecca Killian  
Also present:  Ilona Blanchard, South Burlington Community Development Director 
(Committee Staff).  
1. The meeting was called to order by Nicole LaBrecque, Chair, at 5:30 p.m. Emergency 
exit procedures were reviewed. The agenda was approved (moved by John Burton, 
seconded by Chris Carrigan) unanimously.  
2. Comments from the Public. No members of the public were present; no public comment 
was offered. 
3. Updates: 
 Chair (Nicole LaBrecque):  
o Significant activity at Beta Technologies, including an infusion of funding for 
parts, marketing, and exports that is moving permit work forward; the master 
plan is expected before the board for approval soon.  
o PC Construction is seeking a new site in South Burlington for future 
expansion and housing development. 
 Staff (Ilona Blanchard): Reported on several items: 
o Economic Development Executive Director search: ~12 applicants received; 
6–7 to be interviewed, followed by second-round of interviews. 
o Cymone (Upward Mobility / Economic Development): a morning session on 
“10 legal things every small business owner should know” is being marketed 
to small businesses and entrepreneurs. 
o South Burlington City Center Collaborative (SBCCC): August 27th, 5:30–
7:00 PM at Comfort Suites; the owner of Leunig’s will speak. 
o Market Street business openings: Align Workout — the corridor is expanding 
from food into retail. Chris brought up VT Flannel, a recent lead he had 
provided.
Economic Development Committee Meeting Minutes | Page 2 
o San Remo Area-Wide Plan: the City is working with property owners in 
partnership with CCRPC on brownfield assessment in preparation for funding, 
restoration, and remediation to prepare sites for redevelopment (Part 1). Part 2 
will work directly with owners on a shared vision for the area. 
o Redevelopment of City Center and surrounding neighborhoods remains a top 
city priority. 
o Pedestrian Bridge construction is underway; a weekly email blast will support 
future closure notices. Groundbreaking was well received; projected 
completion in 2028. 
o UVM students (undergraduates) move into Market Street apartments the 
weekend of August 22nd. Graduates and employees already occupy three 
buildings. 
o A peddlers’-ordinance concept for food-truck permitting around City Center 
remains on pause due to staffing changes. 
o South Burlington did not receive Plan of the Year but was recognized with 
kudos. 
 Member Committee Activities: Members shared updates: 
Chris:  
o 
o 
Paige:  
o Met with Hello Burlington, a privately funded regional tourism marketing 
entity. Tourism generated $4.2B statewide in 2024 ($1.03B in Chittenden 
County); South Burlington leads in hotel rooms and rental cars. Potential 
partnership opportunities around hospitality, lodging, and mobility data are 
being explored.  
o SB3C is moving into development of its strategic plan. 
 Council: No council present. 
4. Officer Elections 
Officers were elected unanimously (moved by John Burton, seconded by Paige Brochu) 
as follows: Nicole LaBrecque — Chair and Chris Carrigan — Vice Chair. The Clerk 
position was tabled for September meeting. 
5. Green Community Festival — September 19, 2026
Economic Development Committee Meeting Minutes | Page 3 
The Committee discussed the festival, a day-long event centered on energy and green 
companies with children’s activities and informational booths (formerly the Energy 
Festival, now in its third or fourth year). https://www.southburlingtonvt.gov/701/Green-
Community-Festival 
Action item: Reach out to “green” companies — including technology, farm-to-plate, and 
sustainable-process businesses — to invite participation. The event is not seeking 
significant funding. Members will consult the South Burlington website and email 
Bettina to coordinate. 
6. Economic Development Strategic Plan 
Work Session (telling the story to the community): Broader strategic-plan work is being 
held pending the new Executive Director. 
Innovation District & Aviation Sector: Collins Aerospace was acquired by Simmons, part 
of broader aviation-sector changes. Workforce development continues, with Burlington 
Technical Center training the next generation of technicians through apprenticeships. 
Hospitality/Destination: No updates. 
Permit Expediting/Concierge Permitting: No updates. 
7. Annual Report FY2026 
Nicole LaBrecque has been drafting the FY26 annual report and will have a draft ready 
for the September meeting. 
A committee photo will be taken at the September meeting. 
8. Other Business 
None. 
9. Adjournment 
The meeting was adjourned at approximately 6:30PM (moved by Harold Hershberg, seconded by 
John Burton). 
Paige Brochu
